$comment: The canonical copy of every machine-readable ecosystem fact. A skill's prose, routing table, or ecosystem file may restate a manifest signal, a lockfile name, or a Tidelift platform string, because a single-skill install does not carry this file. On any disagreement this file wins and the skill text is corrected to it. `lockfiles` records what the ecosystem's build tooling produces, which is what R-SEC-08's exemption keys on: an array of filenames means it is produced by default; `mode: opt-in` means the tool can produce one and does not unless asked; `mode: per-tool` means the answer differs by build tool, and only a tool whose `files` is empty takes the exemption; `libraryConvention` records where the ecosystem's own documentation tells a library package not to commit the file, which R-SEC-08's commit-convention clause reaches.

lockfiles.enabledBy: the MSBuild property RestorePackagesWithLockFile, or an existing packages.lock.json in the project root
lockfiles.libraryConvention: NuGet documents that a library project other people depend on should not check the lock file in, and that an application at the start of the dependency chain should.

maven.note: Apache Maven publishes no lockfile format, opt-in or otherwise. It offers fixed versions, dependencyManagement, and enforcer rules such as banDynamicVersions instead. Maven Resolver's Trusted Checksums still record a committed coreutils-format hash file under .mvn/checksums/, verified at resolution with aether.artifactResolver.postProcessor.trustedChecksums.failIfMissing.

gradle.note: Opt-in per configuration through resolutionStrategy.activateDependencyLocking() or dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() }, written with --write-locks. The generated file's own header says it is expected to be part of source control, and a version mismatch already fails the build without an extra flag. Dependency verification is a separate feature, enabled by the presence of gradle/verification-metadata.xml and strict by default.

lockfiles.libraryConvention: Dart documents that an application package should check the lockfile into source control and a regular (library) package should not, because a library is expected to work with a range of dependency versions.

containers.title: Container images
containers.note: Detected by a registry push, never by a Dockerfile: a workflow pushing to a registry, or an existing image on the forge's registry. A Dockerfile more often builds a test harness than a shipped image.
